segments.text: in this video I want to answer the
question what is the voice of the
customer voice of the customer is a
process for systematically listening to
the perceptions the needs the wishes the
expectations and the fears of your
customers and end-users in project
management terms your stakeholders we
use voice of the customer to ensure that
the products the services the new
processes that we are creating will
actually meet their needs and therefore
be used by our end-users our customers
our stakeholders the alternative is we
create what we think they need and it
doesn't match their expectations it
doesn't meet their needs and therefore
it doesn't get used
a formal definition of the voice of the
customer would be something like this
actual customer descriptions in their
own words for the functions and features
they desire for the goods and services
they need a large part of product or
process development in the early stages
is the translation of what you learn in
the voice of the customer process into
formal functional requirements and then
into technical specifications methods of
the gathering voice of the customer
information include one-to-one
interviews surveys and questionnaires
and focus groups that bring together
multiple customers at the same time and
these can be particularly valuable
because the interactions between those
customers bring up new ideas
voice of the customer originates in
product development but for us as
project managers voice of the customer
is also a powerful technique for
stakeholder engagement it's particularly
useful where the uptake of the products
or the processes that we're producing is
discretionary to some extent and
therefore for the end-users to take him
up properly means that we need to
specify them in a way that will satisfy
the needs of those end-users and it's
also important where your end users will
have a strong perspective on how
processes need to work of what products
need to do in order for them to serve
their customers their clients put simply
if you offer your customers or your
end-users something that they really
want they'll buy it and they'll use it
but if you don't if you merely offer
them something you think they want and
you get it wrong all you'll do is
produce an expensive white elephant if
